skill.name: Parallel Logging Batch Coordination with Minimum Timestamp Enforcement
skill.description: Coordinates worker threads to compute and enforce minimum commit timestamps for new log batches, ensuring inter-batch ordering while allowing intra-batch parallelism. Enables scalable crash recovery in multi-core DBMS by batching log writes across multiple files while maintaining correct transaction ordering.
skill.skill_body:
When starting a new log batch: (1) coordinate all worker threads to compute the minimum commit timestamp that is strictly greater than all commit timestamps in the previous batch; (2) enforce this minimum timestamp for all transactions in the new batch; (3) write logs from the new batch to multiple files in parallel; (4) mark the batch as durable only after all log files have been written. Timestamps only increase in this process, so correctness is preserved.

## Objective

Establish durable batch boundaries with correct timestamp ordering across parallel log files
## Applicable Signals

- Previous batch has completed and all logs are durable
- New transactions are ready to enter a new batch
- Multi-core system requires parallel logging for bandwidth

## Contraindications

- Single-log ARIES approach is sufficient for the workload
- Bandwidth constraints do not require parallel logging
- System does not support multi-file concurrent writes

## Workflow Steps

- {'step': 1, 'action': 'Coordinate all worker threads', 'detail': 'Each worker thread reports the maximum commit timestamp of transactions in the previous batch'}
- {'step': 2, 'action': 'Compute minimum commit timestamp for new batch', 'detail': 'Set minimum_ts to a value strictly greater than the maximum commit timestamp from the previous batch'}
- {'step': 3, 'action': 'Enforce minimum timestamp', 'detail': 'Assign all transactions in the new batch a commit timestamp >= minimum_ts'}
- {'step': 4, 'action': 'Write logs in parallel', 'detail': 'Distribute log entries from the new batch across multiple log files and write concurrently'}
- {'step': 5, 'action': 'Verify durability', 'detail': 'Confirm that all log files have been written; mark batch as durable only after all writes complete'}

## Constraints

- All transactions in a later batch must have commit timestamps strictly greater than all transactions in the previous batch
- Relative ordering among transactions within the same batch can be arbitrary
- A batch is durable only after all logs within that batch have been written to all files
- Each worker thread must participate in minimum timestamp computation

## Cautions

- Ensure all worker threads coordinate before computing minimum timestamp; missing coordination can violate inter-batch ordering
- Do not allow transactions to commit with timestamps less than or equal to the batch minimum; this breaks the ordering guarantee
- Verify that all log files have been written before marking a batch as durable

## Output Contract

- New batch minimum timestamp is computed and enforced
- All transactions in the batch have commit_ts > previous batch maximum commit_ts
- Logs are written to multiple files in parallel
- Batch is marked durable only after all log files are persisted

## Example Executions

### Example 1

- Input: Previous batch completed with max commit_ts = 1000; 4 worker threads ready to start new batch
- Output: Minimum timestamp for new batch set to 1001; all new transactions assigned commit_ts >= 1001; logs written to 4 parallel files; batch marked durable after all files persist
- Notes: Ensures strict ordering: all transactions in new batch have higher timestamps than previous batch

### Example 2

- Input: Worker threads report previous batch max timestamps: 1000, 998, 1002, 999
- Output: Global maximum is 1002; new batch minimum_ts set to 1003; all worker threads enforce this minimum for their transactions
- Notes: Coordination step ensures no transaction in new batch can have timestamp <= 1002
